::: {.cell}

:::



[⏱ 30 min]{.timing}

::: {.main-message}
Spatial data are already a representation. Someone decided how location was recorded, and in what coordinate system.
:::

## Load


::: {.cell caption='Run me first'}
```{webr}
#| caption: "Run me first"
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

data_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/maczokni/crime_mapping_workshop/main/data/"
crimes <- read.csv(paste0(data_url, "crimes.csv"))
head(crimes)
```
:::


## Where is the "where"?

Three columns hold location:

| Column | Structure |
|---|---|
| `longitude`, `latitude` | **point** |
| `location` ("On or near …") | **line** (street) |
| `lsoa21cd` (census area) | **polygon** |


::: {.cell}
```{webr}
crimes |> count(location, sort = TRUE) |> head(8)
```
:::


- "Shopping Area", "Nightclub"? These aren't streets.
- police.uk **snaps crimes to anonymous points** to protect privacy.

::: {.callout-important}
## Think
What has been gained, and lost, in recording these crimes this way?
:::

## Table → spatial object


::: {.cell}
```{webr}
crimes_sf <- st_as_sf(crimes,
                      coords = c("longitude", "latitude"),
                      crs = 4326)    # WGS 84: degrees
crimes_sf
```
:::


## First map


::: {.cell}
```{webr}
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = crimes_sf, alpha = 0.3)
```
:::


## Add polygons

- Census areas (**LSOAs**). The shape is stored as text (WKT) in a `geometry` column:


::: {.cell}
```{webr}
lsoa <- read.csv(paste0(data_url, "lsoa.csv")) |>
  st_as_sf(wkt = "geometry", crs = 27700)   # British National Grid: metres

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = lsoa, fill = "white") +
  geom_sf(data = crimes_sf, alpha = 0.3, colour = "#5b2a86") +
  theme_void()
```
:::


- More usual: `st_read("file.shp")` or `.geojson`. Same result.

## CRS


::: {.cell}
```{webr}
st_crs(crimes_sf)$input
st_crs(lsoa)$input
st_crs(crimes_sf) == st_crs(lsoa)
```
:::


- Different CRSs. Transform to match before combining layers.


::: {.cell}
```{webr}
crimes_bng <- st_transform(crimes_sf, 27700)

st_coordinates(crimes_sf)[1, ]   # degrees
st_coordinates(crimes_bng)[1, ]  # metres
```
:::


::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## From GIS?
- `st_as_sf(coords =)` = *Add Delimited Text Layer*
- `st_crs()` = *Layer Properties → CRS*
- `st_transform()` = *Reproject Layer*
- Bonus: the script is your record. Re-run with next month's data.
:::

## Your turn

Map **bicycle thefts** over the LSOAs.


::: {.cell setup='true' exercise='ex_bike'}
```{webr}
#| setup: true
#| exercise: ex_bike
library(sf); library(dplyr); library(ggplot2)
data_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/maczokni/crime_mapping_workshop/main/data/"
crimes_bng <- read.csv(paste0(data_url, "crimes.csv")) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326) |>
  st_transform(27700)
lsoa <- read.csv(paste0(data_url, "lsoa.csv")) |> st_as_sf(wkt = "geometry", crs = 27700)
```
:::



::: {.cell exercise='ex_bike'}
```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_bike
bikes <- crimes_bng |>
  filter(crime_type == "______")

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = lsoa, fill = "white", colour = "grey70") +
  geom_sf(data = ______, colour = "red") +
  theme_void()
```
:::


::: {.hint exercise="ex_bike"}
`"Bicycle theft"`. Second layer: `bikes`.
:::

::: {.solution exercise="ex_bike"}
```r
bikes <- crimes_bng |> filter(crime_type == "Bicycle theft")

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = lsoa, fill = "white", colour = "grey70") +
  geom_sf(data = bikes, colour = "red") +
  theme_void()
```
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Know R?
- `facet_wrap(~ crime_type)` for small multiples of 4–5 crime types.
- Distance from each theft to St Peter's Square: `st_point(c(-2.2433, 53.4781))`, then `st_sfc(crs = 4326)`, `st_transform()` and `st_distance()`.
:::
